items.title: Steam Client is now faster than Epic's new vibe coded launcher

extra.evidence: Yesterday, Epic Games announced and launched in preview its new vibe-coded launcher. The main marketing pitch was a jab at Steam’s slow loading speed compared to the new Epic launcher. Well,… this is such a good day to be a sweeney hater.. not even 24h later lmao https://t.co/hjf5Q9NV3C pic.twitter.com/XXLcIqYTT7 On basic test systems, Valve’s client boot time dropped to 5.23 seconds, beating Epic’s new launcher and neutralizing its primary performance claim. While Epic Games Launcher V2 remains, a massive step forward compared to its notoriously sluggish legacy build, Valve demonstrated how quickly it can react to competitive benchmarks. Epic may have “vibe coded” a faster client, but Valve proved that targeted optimization on a decades-old ecosystem can still beat out AI speedruns. But…

items.title: Proof-based general-purpose computing with Magnetar
items.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs can verify computing results without rerunning workloads or exposing sensitive data. Magnetar helps bring them into the mainstream with support for standard programming languages, major speed gains, and quantum-resistant security. The post Proof-based general-purpose computing with Magnetar appeared first on Microsoft Research .

items.title: Muse Spark Open is Meta's answer to Qwen, GLM, and Kimi in the open-weight race
items.summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open is a new open-weight model with 816 billion parameters that processes text, images, video, and audio with up to one million tokens of context. It performs roughly on par with the most capable open-weight Chinese AI models on benchmarks and is optimized to run locally on Apple's M5 Ultra. The article Muse Spark Open is Meta's answer to Qwen, GLM, and Kimi in the open-weight race appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: ggml-org/llama.cpp v0.7.0

extra.evidence: ## Overview llama.cpp v0.7.0 adds the LiliCorr speculative decoding technique and MTP for GLM5-Next, a new GPU cache for MoE experts kept in host memory (`--moe-cache-mib`, up to ~2.2x decode speedup when experts are offloaded), and a large batch of new models: K2 Horizon (dense and MoVA), Prism Bonsai 2 27B, EmbeddingGemma-2 (text+vision+audio), the LiquidAI d1/d1-omni and vLLM decision 2/d3 decision models, pplx-decider, MiniCPM-V 4.7, Nemotron Super 3.5 VL / Nemotron Bolt and maion-coder. The server gets a refactored chat session API (`common_chat_session`, part-based formatted output), much better slot and prompt-cache restore behavior, decision-model support for the new architectures and a new default port (9931), the web UI gains a full models manager, and ggml is updated to v0.27.0. ### Highlights - New GPU cache for host-memory MoE experts (`--moe-cache-mib`): experts run on the GPU from an LRU cache, up to 2.2x faster decode [#29887](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887) - The expert cache is now shared across multiple GPUs [#30112](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30112) - LiliCorr speculative decoding: candidate selection with a small draft transformer on top of DFlash [#30506](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/30506) - GLM5-Next: MTP speculative decoding with an optimized sparse attention path [#29928](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29928) - K2 Horizon support in both dense and MoVA variants: conversion, tokenizer, chat…

items.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
items.summary: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. Existing benchmarks measure downstream task success under a fixed harness, leaving harness engineering itself unexplored. We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly. In Stage 1, a build model operating inside a fixed builder harness receives an interface-only contract skeleton and a development document tha…

items.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
items.summary: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. However, games, with their visually rich worlds and diverse mechanics, remain challenging and offer a demanding next step toward general digital control. Current game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic game states, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain. We introduce Player-1, a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic…

items.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
items.summary: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-…

items.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) routing distributes inference work across different models, advancing the cost-quality Pareto frontier of LLM serving. While coarse-grained routing at the session or query level has been widely adopted in production systems, recent algorithmic work shows that fine-grained token-level routing can yield substantial efficiency and quality gains. However, efficiently serving token-level routed inference poses significant challenges to existing systems. Built on single-LLM assumptions, current systems suffer from severe step desynchronization and frequent batch admission…

items.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) by routing domain-specific data to specialized teachers, integrating their capabilities through dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, domain routing only distinguishes the supervision sources for different domains; updates from all domains still act on shared parameters.
